To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the synthesis of a series of new 2-{[E)-3-arylprop-2-enyl]amino} benzoic amides was accomplished by a simple and efficient method and that the most active compounds in the series were found to act as antitumor agents by interfering with the microtubule cytoskeleton.
a series of 17 new compounds was synthesized and evaluated as antiproliferatives against a full NCI panel of cancer cell lines.
a series of new 2-{((2E)-3-(4-substituted phenyl)prop-2-enyl)amino}benzoic acids were synthesized and evaluated for in vitro antip proliferative activity against a panel of 60 cancer cell lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis, and antitubulin antiproliferation activity of a new series of 2-[(E)-3-arylprop-2-en-1-oyl]amides.
the synthesis of a series of new compounds with a 2-{[(E)-3-arylp-2-enoy]amino}phenyl moiety.
the development of a series of new compounds that can be considered as potential antitubulin drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new compounds act as tubulin polymerization inhibitors, which in turn results in cell cycle arrest and apoptosis.
the new compounds 12a-s, 17t, and 17v are antiproliferatives, with 17t and 17v being the most active, and they act through a tubulin polymerization mechanism.
the new 2-{[E]-3-phenyl-2-propenoates}benzamidines are a new class of antiproliferatives with potential clinical utility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

2-{[(E)-3- phenylprop-2-enoate]amino}anilides 12 are a new class of antitubulin antiproliferatives with a novel structure and a mechanism of action different from those of the known antitubulin drugs, paclitaxel and epothilones.

2-{[(E)-3-arylprop-2-en-1-oyl]amido}benzoic acids are potent tubulin polymerization inhibitors and that the antiproliferation effect observed in cells is due to the ability of these compounds to induce tubulin depolymerization.

the new 2-{(2E)-3-substituted propenoic acid}amides 12 and 17, which were prepared from the corresponding 3-substituted acrylic acid chlorides and 5-iodothranilamide, are potent antiproliferatives with activity in the sub-micromolar range against a number of cancer cell lines, and they act by disrupting microtubules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antiproliferation of these new benzamides is not only due to their ability to bind to tubulin, but also to the ability of their phenyl rings to interact with tubulin.
the presence of a 4-methoxy group in the aromatic ring of the (E)-2-aminocinnamic amide is a prerequisite for antiproliferation.
the presence of a 4-methylphenyl group at the 3-position of the phenylacrylic acid is a key feature of antitubulin activity.
